nodes.summary: For a sequence $s = d_1, \dots, d_k$ of dominoes, the bottom word of $s$ is the concatenation $b_1 b_2 \cdots b_k$, where $b_i$ is the bottom word of $d_i$.
nodes.title: Bottom word of a domino sequence

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with a finite tape alphabet $\Gamma$, a default (blank) symbol $\beta \in \Gamma$ and finitely many states. The symbols are the tape symbols, the states, the end markers $\vdash$ and $\dashv$, and the halting symbol $H$. Every rule $l \to r$ of the rewriting system simulating $M$ has one of the following eight forms, where $q, q'$ are states and $a, b, c$ are tape symbols.…
nodes.title: The eight kinds of rules of the machine-simulating rewriting system

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter whose elements have a computable encoding. Then the Post correspondence problem over $\alpha$ is a computable predicate: some computable function decides, for every finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, whether $P$ has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: PCP over a one-letter alphabet is decidable

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol $H$ control symbols. Consider the relation in which a word $w$ with exactly one control symbol rewrites to $w'$ by one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$. This relation is confluent: if $w$ rewrites in zero or more such steps to both $w_1$ and $w_2$, then $w_1$ and $w_2$ both…
nodes.title: The rewrites from words with one control symbol are confluent

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol $H$ control symbols. If a word $w$ rewrites to $w'$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$, then $w$ and $w'$ contain the same number of control symbols.
nodes.title: Rewriting preserves the number of control symbols

nodes.summary: The number of control symbols of a word $w$ over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine is the number of letters of $w$ that are states or the halting symbol $H$.
nodes.title: Number of control symbols

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol $H$ control symbols. A word $w$ rewrites to $w'$ by a controlled step when $w$ contains exactly one control symbol and $w$ rewrites to $w'$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$.
nodes.title: Rewrites from words with one control symbol

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $\vdash$, $\dashv$ be the end markers and $H$ the halting symbol of the rewriting system simulating $M$. For all words $X$ and $Y$ of tape symbols, the word $\vdash X\,H\,Y \dashv$ rewrites in zero or more steps of this rewriting system to the halting word $\vdash H \dashv$.
nodes.title: The halting symbol erases the tape

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $\vdash$, $\dashv$ be the end markers and $H$ the halting symbol of the rewriting system simulating $M$. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ at which $M$ has no next step, and let $w$ be a word that spells $c$: for some state $q$, tape symbol $h$ and lists $L$, $R$ of tape symbols, $c$ is in state $q$ with $h$ under the head,…
nodes.title: A halted configuration rewrites to the halting word

nodes.summary: A domino over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a pair $(t, b)$ of words over $\alpha$: its top word $t$ and its bottom word $b$.
nodes.title: Domino (Post correspondence problem)

nodes.summary: Over the alphabet $\alpha$ extended with the star $\star$ and the end marker $\diamond$, the end domino is $(\star\diamond, \diamond)$: its top word is $\star$ followed by $\diamond$, and its bottom word is $\diamond$.
nodes.title: End domino of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction

nodes.summary: The end marker $\diamond$ is the symbol of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction that is neither a letter of $\alpha$ nor the star $\star$.
nodes.title: End marker

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of the elements of a type $\alpha$, let $A$ and $B$ be lists over $\alpha$ none of whose elements satisfy $P$, and let $y \in \alpha$. If $C$ and $D$ are lists over $\alpha$ and $x \in \alpha$ satisfies $P$ with $C\,x\,D = A\,y\,B$ (concatenation), then $C = A$, $x = y$ and $D = B$.
nodes.title: Unique splitting at a marked letter

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and call the states and the halting symbol $H$ control symbols. Suppose $w$ contains exactly one control symbol, and $w$ and $w'$ are equivalent under the equivalence relation generated by one-step rewriting in the rewriting system simulating $M$. Then $w$ and $w'$ are equivalent under the equivalence relation generated by the…
nodes.title: Thue equivalence from a word with one control symbol uses only controlled steps

nodes.summary: For a finite tape alphabet $\Gamma$, let $H$ be the halting symbol of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine with tape alphabet $\Gamma$. The erasing rules are the rewriting rules $c\,H \to H$ and $H\,c \to H$ for every tape symbol $c \in \Gamma$: the halting symbol deletes the tape symbol on either side of it.
nodes.title: Erasing rules

nodes.summary: (Post, Markov) There are a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, and a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, whether $x$ and $y$ are equivalent under the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R$.
nodes.title: Some finite Thue system has an undecidable word problem

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for a finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, whether every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom and $P$ has a solution of the modified Post correspondence problem, that is, a nonempty sequence of dominoes of $P$, repetitions allowed, that…
nodes.title: MPCP is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides whether a finite list of dominoes over $\alpha$ has a solution, that is, a nonempty sequence of dominoes of the list, repetitions allowed, whose tops and bottoms concatenate to the same word.
nodes.title: The Post correspondence problem is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, whether every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.
nodes.title: Reachability for string rewriting is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $\alpha$, with a primitive recursive coding of its letters by natural numbers, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for a finite list $R$ of rewriting rules over $\alpha$ and words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, whether $x$ and $y$ are equivalent under the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R$.
nodes.title: The uniform word problem for Thue systems is undecidable

nodes.summary: If a word $w$ over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine contains exactly one control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol), then $w = p\,x\,s$ for a control symbol $x$ and words $p$ and $s$ that contain no control symbol.
nodes.title: A word with one control symbol splits at it

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many tape symbols and states. If the word $w$ spells the configuration $c$ and $M$ steps from $c$ to $c'$, then $w$ rewrites in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$ to a word $w'$ that spells $c'$.
nodes.title: One machine step is one rewrite

nodes.summary: The halting word is the word $\vdash H \dashv$ made of the left end marker, the halting symbol and the right end marker. It is the target word of the rewriting simulation of a single-tape machine.
nodes.title: The halting word

nodes.summary: For an input $l$ of tape symbols, the start word is $\vdash q_0\, h\, R \dashv$, where $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the left and right end markers, $q_0$ is the default state, $h$ is the first symbol of $l$ (the default tape symbol if $l$ is empty) and $R$ is the rest of $l$. It spells the configuration in state $q_0$ with head symbol $h$, empty left part and right part $R$.
nodes.title: The start word

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finitely many tape symbols and states, and $l$ an input. A word $w$ satisfies the invariant for $l$ when either $w$ spells a configuration that $M$ reaches from its initial configuration on $l$, or $M$ halts on $l$ and $w = \vdash X\, H\, Y \dashv$ for some words $X$ and $Y$ of tape symbols, where $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the left and right end markers and $H$ is the halting…
nodes.title: Invariant of the rewriting simulation of a single-tape machine

nodes.summary: The Boolean function on the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape Turing machine that is true on every state symbol and on the halting symbol $H$, and false on every tape symbol and on the end markers $\vdash$ and $\dashv$.
nodes.title: Boolean test for control symbols

nodes.summary: A symbol of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape Turing machine is a control symbol if it is a state symbol or the halting symbol $H$; tape symbols and the end markers $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are not control symbols.
nodes.title: Control symbols

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding and decidable equality, and let $P$ and $s$ be lists of dominoes over $\alpha$. The Boolean solution check of $s$ for $P$ is true exactly when $s$ is nonempty, every domino of $s$ occurs in $P$, and the top word of $s$ equals the bottom word of $s$, and it is false otherwise.
nodes.title: Boolean check for PCP solutions

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite list of dominoes. A solution of $P$ is a nonempty sequence $d_1, \dots, d_k$ of dominoes, each occurring in $P$ (repetitions allowed), such that the concatenation of the top words of $d_1, \dots, d_k$ equals the concatenation of their bottom words.
nodes.title: PCP solution

nodes.summary: Write $|w|$ for the length of a word $w$. Let $s$ be a finite sequence of dominoes over an alphabet. If every domino $(t, b)$ in $s$ satisfies $|b| \le |t|$, then the concatenation of the bottom words of $s$ is no longer than the concatenation of the top words of $s$.
nodes.title: Total length of dominoes that are at least as long on top

nodes.summary: Write $|w|$ for the length of a word $w$. Let $s$ be a nonempty finite sequence of dominoes over an alphabet. If every domino $(t, b)$ in $s$ satisfies $|b| < |t|$, then the concatenation of the bottom words of $s$ is strictly shorter than the concatenation of the top words of $s$.
nodes.title: Total length of dominoes that are strictly longer on top

nodes.summary: Each letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$ is regarded as a symbol of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction, which consists of the letters of $\alpha$, the star $\star$ and the end marker $\diamond$.
nodes.title: The alphabet inside the extended alphabet

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ over the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction, this is the word over $\alpha$ obtained from $w$ by deleting every star $\star$ and every end marker $\diamond$, keeping the letters of $\alpha$ in their order.
nodes.title: Erasing stars and end markers

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding, and let $\alpha'$ be $\alpha$ extended with two new symbols, the star and the end marker. There is a computable function $f$ from finite lists of dominoes over $\alpha$ to finite lists of dominoes over $\alpha'$ such that, for every list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, $f(P)$ has a PCP solution if and only if both every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top…
nodes.title: MPCP many-one reduces to PCP

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding of its letters as natural numbers. Then the Post correspondence problem over $\alpha$ is many-one reducible to the Post correspondence problem over the two-letter alphabet of Booleans $\mathrm{true}$ and $\mathrm{false}$: there is a computable map $f$ sending each finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$ to a finite list $f(P)$ of dominoes over…
nodes.title: PCP over a finite alphabet many-one reduces to PCP over the binary alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $R_M$ be the rewriting system simulating $M$. Then the set of inputs on which $M$ halts is many-one reducible to the set of pairs $(x, y)$ of words over the symbols of $R_M$ that are equivalent under the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step rewriting by $R_M$.
nodes.title: Single-tape halting many-one reduces to the word problem of a fixed Thue system

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols. Then the set of inputs on which $M$ halts is many-one reducible to the set of instances $(R, x, y)$, where $R$ is a list of rules and $x$, $y$ are words over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating $M$, such that every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side and $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps…
nodes.title: Single-tape halting many-one reduces to string rewriting reachability

nodes.summary: For a word $u$ over $\alpha$, write $\star u$ for the word over the extended alphabet obtained by putting a star $\star$ before every letter of $u$, and $u\star$ for the word obtained by putting a star after every letter. A domino $(t, b)$ over $\alpha$ is sent to the domino $(\star t, b\star)$ over the extended alphabet.
nodes.title: Starred image of a domino

nodes.summary: Given a map $f$ from words over $\alpha$ to words over $\beta$ and a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the image of $P$ under $f$ is the list of dominoes over $\beta$ obtained by replacing each domino $(u, v)$ of $P$ by $(f(u), f(v))$, in the same order.
nodes.title: Image of a PCP instance under a word map

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over an alphabet $\alpha$ in which every domino has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom. Then $P$ has an MPCP solution if and only if the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP, an instance over $\alpha$ extended with a star and an end marker, has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: MPCP reduces to PCP on instances with nonempty words

nodes.summary: On instances with nonempty words, a PCP solution of the reduced instance gives an MPCP solution. Let $P$ be a list of dominoes in which every domino has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom. If the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP has a PCP solution, then $P$ has an MPCP solution.
nodes.title: On instances with nonempty words, a PCP solution of the reduced instance gives an MPCP solution

nodes.summary: A list $P$ of dominoes has an MPCP solution when $P$ is nonempty and some PCP solution of $P$ starts with the first domino of $P$.
nodes.title: The modified Post correspondence problem

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and let $\sqcup$ be its blank symbol. For words $u$, $v$ and a state $q$, the successor of $u\,q\,v$ is defined as follows. If $v$ does not begin with a tape symbol, there is none. If $v = a\,v'$ for a tape symbol $a$: when $M$ has no transition from $q$ reading $a$, it is $u\,H\,v'$, where $H$ is the halting symbol; when $M$ writes…

nodes.summary: For a list $P$ of dominoes, this Boolean test returns true exactly when every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom.

nodes.summary: A list $P$ of dominoes has nonempty words when every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top word and a nonempty bottom word.
nodes.title: Instances with nonempty words

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols. There is no word $w$ such that the halting word $\vdash H \dashv$ rewrites to $w$ in one step of the rewriting system simulating $M$.
nodes.title: The halting word is irreducible

nodes.summary: The Post correspondence problem over the two-letter alphabet of Booleans $\mathrm{true}$ and $\mathrm{false}$, that is, the property of a finite list $P$ of dominoes over the Booleans of having a PCP solution, is not decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine: no multi-stack machine computes a total function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every such $P$ with natural-number encoding $n_P$,…
nodes.title: The Post correspondence problem is undecidable over the binary alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter, and write $|w|$ for the length of a word $w$. A finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$ has a PCP solution if and only if either some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| = |b|$, or some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| < |b|$ and some domino $(t', b')$ in $P$ has $|b'| < |t'|$.
nodes.title: The unary PCP criterion

nodes.summary: Let $h$ map each letter of $\alpha$ to a word over $\beta$, and extend it to words by $h(a_1 \cdots a_n) = h(a_1) \cdots h(a_n)$. If this extension is injective on words over $\alpha$, then for every list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the list obtained from $P$ by replacing each domino $(u, v)$ by $(h(u), h(v))$ has a PCP solution if and only if $P$ has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: An injective word homomorphism preserves and reflects PCP solvability

nodes.summary: If a list $P$ of dominoes has an MPCP solution, then the image of $P$ under the reduction from MPCP to PCP has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: An MPCP solution gives a PCP solution of the reduced instance

nodes.summary: A list $P$ of dominoes is a solvable instance of the Post correspondence problem when it has a PCP solution: a nonempty sequence of dominoes from $P$, repetitions allowed, whose top words and bottom words concatenate to the same word.
nodes.title: The Post correspondence problem

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive coding, the Boolean test of whether every domino of a list over $\alpha$ has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom is a primitive recursive function of the list.
nodes.title: The nonempty-words test is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive coding, the set of lists of dominoes over $\alpha$ that have a PCP solution is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: PCP is recursively enumerable

nodes.summary: For a list $P$ of dominoes, the total reduction sends $P$ to its image under the reduction from MPCP to PCP when every domino of $P$ has a nonempty top and a nonempty bottom, and to the empty instance, which has no PCP solution, otherwise.
nodes.title: The total reduction from MPCP to PCP

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, let $\sqcup$ be its blank symbol, and write $\vdash$, $\dashv$ for the end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. The rules for a state $q$ reading a tape symbol $a$ are: the rule $q\,a \to H$ if $M$ has no transition from $q$ reading $a$; the rule $q\,a \to q'\,b$ if $M$ writes $b$ and enters $q'$; the rules…
nodes.title: The rules for one transition

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, and write $H$ for the halting symbol. The rewriting system simulating $M$ is the finite list of rules consisting of the rules for every state $q$ reading every tape symbol $a$, followed by the erasing rules $c\,H \to H$ and $H\,c \to H$ for every tape symbol $c$.
nodes.title: The rewriting system simulating a Turing machine

nodes.summary: For a state $q$, a tape symbol $h$ and words $L$, $R$ of tape symbols, the word of the configuration in state $q$ with head symbol $h$, left part $L$ (in reading order, from left to right) and right part $R$ is $\vdash L\,q\,h\,R \dashv$, where $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ are the end markers.
nodes.title: The word of a configuration

nodes.summary: A word $w$ spells a configuration $c$ of a single-tape Turing machine if there are a state $q$, a tape symbol $h$ and words $L$, $R$ of tape symbols such that $c$ is in state $q$, its head reads $h$, its tape reads $L$ immediately to the left of the head and $R$ immediately to the right of it, with blanks beyond, and $w = \vdash L\,q\,h\,R \dashv$.
nodes.title: Words spelling a configuration

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $u$, $v$, $p$, $s$ be words over the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine, and let $x$ and $y$ be symbols. If no symbol of $A$ or of $B$ is a control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol), $x$ is a control symbol, and $u\,p\,x\,s\,v = A\,y\,B$, then $u\,p = A$, $x = y$ and $s\,v = B$.
nodes.title: Splitting a rewrite site at its control symbol

nodes.summary: Let $\star$ be the star of the extended alphabet. For a word $u = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$, the word $u\star$ over the extended alphabet is $a_1 \star a_2 \star \cdots a_n \star$, obtained by putting a star after every letter of $u$; the empty word gives the empty word.
nodes.title: A star after every letter

nodes.summary: Let $\star$ be the star of the extended alphabet. For a word $u = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$, the word $\star u$ over the extended alphabet is $\star a_1 \star a_2 \cdots \star a_n$, obtained by putting a star before every letter of $u$; the empty word gives the empty word.
nodes.title: A star before every letter

nodes.summary: The star $\star$ is the new symbol of the extended alphabet that is neither a letter of $\alpha$ nor the end marker $\diamond$.
nodes.title: The star symbol

nodes.summary: For a domino $(t, b)$ over an alphabet $\alpha$, its start domino is the domino $(\star t, \star b \star)$ over the extended alphabet, where $\star t$ puts the star $\star$ before every letter of $t$ and $b \star$ puts a star after every letter of $b$, so that the bottom word gets one extra star in front.
nodes.title: The start domino of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and let $w$ be a word over the symbols of its rewriting system that contains exactly one control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol). If $w$ rewrites in one step to $w_1$ and in one step to $w_2$ under the rules of $M$, then there is a word $d$ such that $w_1$ rewrites to $d$ in at most one step and $w_2$ rewrites to $d$…
nodes.title: Local confluence on words with one control symbol

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states. Let $x$ be a control symbol (a state symbol or the halting symbol $H$) and let $u$ and $v$ be words that contain no control symbol. If $u\,x\,v$ rewrites in one step to $w'$ under the rules of $M$, then either $x$ is a state symbol $q$ and the successor of $u\,q\,v$ under the rules for $q$ is defined and equals $w'$, or $x = H$ and…
nodes.title: A rewrite at the control symbol

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and let $l$ be an input word. Write $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. A word $w$ satisfies the invariant for $M$ and $l$ when either $w$ spells a configuration that $M$ reaches from its initial configuration on $l$ (the configuration with state $q$, head symbol $h$, left part…
nodes.title: Every rewrite preserves the invariant of reachable words

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $s$ of dominoes, the swapped sequence is obtained from $s$ by exchanging the top and bottom word of every domino: each $(t, b)$ becomes $(b, t)$, and the order of the dominoes is unchanged.
nodes.title: Swapping top and bottom

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the extended alphabet consists of the letters of $\alpha$ together with two new symbols: the star $\star$ and the end marker $\diamond$.
nodes.title: The extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine with finite tape alphabet and finite set of states, and write $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol. For every input word $l$, $M$ halts on $l$ if and only if the start word ${\vdash}\,q_0\,h\,R\,{\dashv}$ of $l$ rewrites to the halting word ${\vdash}\,H\,{\dashv}$ in zero or more steps under the rules of $M$, where $q_0$ is the…
nodes.title: A single-tape machine halts iff its start word rewrites to the halting word

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with finitely many states and tape symbols, write $\vdash$ and $\dashv$ for the left and right end markers and $H$ for the halting symbol, and let $l$ be an input word of tape symbols. Then $M$ halts on $l$ if and only if the start word of $l$ and the halting word ${\vdash}\,H\,{\dashv}$ are equivalent under the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure of one-step…
nodes.title: A single-tape machine halts iff its start word is Thue equivalent to the halting word

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter whose elements have a computable encoding. Then the Post correspondence problem over $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine: some multi-stack Turing machine decides, for every finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, whether $P$ has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: Unary PCP is decidable by a multi-stack machine

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding, there is a multi-stack Turing machine that, started on the binary encoding of a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, halts exactly when $P$ has a PCP solution.
nodes.title: PCP is Turing-recognizable

nodes.summary: For a tape alphabet $\Gamma$ and a set of states $\Lambda$, the symbols of the rewriting system simulating a single-tape machine are a tape symbol $a$ for each $a \in \Gamma$, a state symbol $q$ for each $q \in \Lambda$, the left end marker $\vdash$, the right end marker $\dashv$ and the halting symbol $H$.

nodes.summary: Write $\star$ for the star and $\diamond$ for the end marker of the extended alphabet; for a word $u$ over $\alpha$, $\star u$ puts a star before every letter of $u$ and $u \star$ puts a star after every letter of $u$. The empty list of dominoes is sent to the empty list. A list $P = [d_0, d_1, \ldots, d_n]$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, with $d_0 = (t_0, b_0)$, is sent to the following list of dominoes over the…
nodes.title: The reduction from MPCP to PCP

nodes.summary: For a sequence of dominoes $(t_1, b_1), \ldots, (t_n, b_n)$, its top word is the concatenation $t_1 t_2 \cdots t_n$ of their top words; the empty sequence has the empty top word.
nodes.title: Top word of a sequence of dominoes

nodes.summary: Given an indexing $e$ assigning a natural number to each letter of $\alpha$, the unary code of a letter $a$ is the Boolean word consisting of $e(a)$ copies of $\mathrm{true}$ followed by one $\mathrm{false}$; writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, it is $1^{e(a)} 0$.
nodes.title: Unary code of a letter

nodes.summary: Let $e$ be an injective map from $\alpha$ to the natural numbers, and let $c(a)$ be the unary code of a letter $a$: $e(a)$ copies of $\mathrm{true}$ followed by one $\mathrm{false}$. Then the map sending a word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$ to the Boolean word $c(a_1) \cdots c(a_n)$ is injective.
nodes.title: The unary code of an injective indexing is uniquely decodable

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with at most one letter, and write $|w|$ for the length of a word $w$. For a finite list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the unary test of $P$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| = |b|$, or some domino $(t, b)$ in $P$ has $|t| < |b|$ and some domino $(t', b')$ in $P$ has $|b'| < |t'|$.
nodes.title: The unary PCP test

nodes.summary: For a domino $(t, b)$ over the extended alphabet, its unmapping is the domino over $\alpha$ obtained by deleting every star $\star$ and every end marker $\diamond$ from both $t$ and $b$, keeping the letters of $\alpha$ in order.
nodes.title: Erasing the markers from a domino
